chunks: 5130 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated that from Abu Ayyub, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: “If a slave confesses against himself to theft, he is not to have his hand cut off; but if two witnesses testify against him, his hand is cut off.”

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: a slave; the legal subject discussed in the ruling
key_terms.شَاهِدَانِ: two witnesses whose testimony establishes the case
key_terms.قُطِعَ: his hand is cut off as the legal punishment
key_terms.لَمْ يُقْطَعْ: the hadd cutting is not carried out on him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave confesses to theft in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning the hadd punishment for theft in the case of a slave. It distinguishes between self-confession and testimony by two witnesses, indicating different evidentiary consequences in judicial application.
